description:
What this shows: Ledger data exchange and object-fetch traffic between this node and its peers: ledger sync, tree-node retrieval, and transaction-set exchange.
Use it to: See how much ledger data the node is pulling or serving and spot catch-up activity.

panels.title: Ledger Data — Ledger
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Inbound bytes for ledger-data message categories, split into aggregate get/share plus the transaction-set, transaction-node, and account-state-node sub-types the node receives from peers.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-category inbound byte rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Normally low and flat once synced. Account-state-node traffic dominates during state sync; transaction-set-candidate traffic dominates during consensus catch-up.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; low and steady on a synced node.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained high account-state or tx-node inbound bytes on a node that should be caught up (repeated re-sync, missing history), or a single peer driving all traffic.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: GetObject — Ledger
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Inbound bytes for object-fetch traffic broken down by object type: ledger headers, individual transactions, transaction-tree nodes, and state-tree nodes.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-type inbound byte rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Small during steady state; grows when the node fetches missing tree nodes.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; low when synced.*

###### Watch for:
*A large share on state/tx nodes for long periods (persistent gap-filling), meaning the node keeps catching up.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:

panels.title: GetObject Messages — Ledger
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Count of individual object-fetch request/response messages per object type.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-type inbound message rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Many messages with few bytes means small piecemeal fetches; few messages with many bytes means large batch transfers.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*High message counts with tiny payloads sustained over time (inefficient per-node fetching).*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:

panels.title: GetObject — Specials
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Aggregate object-fetch inbound bytes plus special buckets: content-addressed storage fetches, bulk fetch-pack downloads used during catch-up, and bulk transaction fetches.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-category inbound byte rate per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Fetch-pack rises sharply while catching up a range of ledgers; near zero when fully synced.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent; low when synced.*

###### Watch for:
*Continuous fetch-pack traffic (node never fully catches up) or unexpectedly high content-store volume.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`

panels.title: Overlay Traffic Heatmap (All Categories, Bytes In)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*All overlay traffic categories ranked by inbound bytes, giving an at-a-glance view of which message types consume the most receive bandwidth.*

###### How it's computed:
*Top categories by latest inbound byte value across all traffic categories.*

###### Reading it:
*The longest bars are the biggest bandwidth consumers; on a synced node transactions, proposals, and validations usually lead.*

###### Healthy range:
*workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A single ledger-data or fetch category dominating (ongoing sync) or an unexpected category topping the list.*

###### Source:
[OverlayImpl.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/OverlayImpl.cpp)

###### Function:
`OverlayImpl ctor (TrafficGauges)`
